d: done with great care and effort
e: The painstaking survey took three years.

d: to reduce the severity of without curing
e: The drug palliates symptoms but does not cure the disease.

d: a perfect example of a quality
e: She was a paragon of patience.
After the scandal he became a pariah in the industry.
The newspaper's parochial focus ignored world events.
The parsimonious owner refused to fix the heating.
The debate was bitterly partisan.
A paucity of evidence weakened the case.

d: too concerned with small details or rules
e: The pedantic reviewer listed every missing comma.
The film's pedestrian plot bored audiences.

d: very clear, in water or in expression
e: Her pellucid prose made a hard subject simple.
He has a penchant for spicy food.

d: extremely poor; or very unwilling to spend
e: The penurious student lived on rice and beans.
The perfidious ally switched sides mid-battle.

d: done quickly and without care or interest
e: He gave the report a perfunctory read.

d: at the edge; of minor importance
e: The peripheral issues were left for later.

d: harmful in a gradual or hidden way
e: The pernicious rumor damaged her career.

d: quick to notice and understand things
e: The perspicacious detective spotted the clue at once.
The phlegmatic goalkeeper never panicked.

d: to calm someone by making concessions
e: The airline placated passengers with vouchers.

d: a dull remark that has been said too often
e: The speech was full of platitudes about teamwork.
A plethora of options confused the shoppers.

d: strongly attacking or defending an opinion
e: Her polemical essay drew angry letters.

d: dealing with things in a practical way
e: A pragmatic solution was better than a perfect one.

d: not secure; likely to fall or fail
e: The climber held a precarious position on the ledge.

d: done suddenly and without careful thought
e: The precipitate decision led to losses.
The injury precluded her from competing.
The precocious child read novels at five.

d: knowing about events before they happen
e: Her prescient warning about the market proved right.

d: to avoid the truth by speaking evasively
e: When pressed, the spokesperson prevaricated.
The forest remained pristine.
The judge was known for her probity.
The prodigal heir spent his fortune in a year.
The government was accused of profligate spending.
Food stalls proliferated around the stadium.

d: a natural tendency to behave in a certain way
e: He has a propensity to exaggerate.

d: to win the favor of someone by pleasing them
e: They tried to propitiate the angry investors with a dividend.
The prosaic report listed facts without insight.
The rules proscribe phones in the exam room.

d: acting with care and thought for the future
e: It is prudent to back up your files.
The pugnacious host interrupted every guest.

d: to limit or modify a statement
e: She qualified her praise by noting the book's length.

d: a state of uncertainty about what to do
e: He was in a quandary over which offer to accept.
The querulous passenger objected to everything.
The disease remained quiescent for years.
His quixotic plan to end all traffic jams never left the drawing board.
The rancor between the families lasted generations.

d: distant from ordinary people; thin, as in air
e: The scholar moved in rarefied academic circles.
The recalcitrant student refused to join any group.
The lecture covered recondite details of ancient law.
The new law aims to redress unfair pay.
The refractory horse threw every rider.
The data refuted the old theory.

d: to move to a lower position
e: The old printer was relegated to the storage room.
The novel's hero is a charming reprobate.

d: to refuse to accept or be linked with
e: The party repudiated the extremist statement.
The council rescinded the parking fee.

d: not revealing thoughts or feelings easily
e: She was reticent about her private life.
